title: The Striker: a name that knocks on the door.
subtitle: One of the names of the Day of Judgement
then: This is one of the earliest surahs revealed in Makkah. It opens with a single word. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Al-Qari'ah is one of the names of the Day of Judgement{/idea}, alongside Al-Haqqah and Al-Ghashiyah. The name itself is a knock: {trap}something that strikes{/trap}.
now: A loud knock at the door at night. Your heart jumps before your mind catches up. The surah starts like that on purpose. {idea}It wants you awake before it tells you anything.{/idea}
old: The Day of Judgement is a distant idea I can think about later.
new: It is named for how it arrives: a sudden blow. Better to wake up now.
try: When you hear a knock or a doorbell today, let it remind you to be ready for the Day.

title: What is the Striker? The question repeats.
subtitle: A pause that makes you listen
then: Maududi says the surah first {idea}alerts and alarms the listeners{/idea} with the name, then the question, then another question, before describing anything. The Makkans who heard it {trap}were being prepared for dreadful news{/trap}.
now: A doctor sits down and says, I need to talk to you about something. Your whole body listens. {idea}This verse is that sitting down.{/idea} Allah is asking for all of your attention before He speaks.
old: I already know what the Day of Judgement is.
new: Allah asks the question because I do not really know it yet.
try: Read this surah once today slowly, pausing after each question.

title: Nothing you know can tell you what it is.
subtitle: Beyond anything we have experienced

key.label: What we can compare it to

then: Ibn Kathir says with this question Allah {trap}intensifies concern and fright{/trap} for the Day. Only after three steps of build-up does He {idea}explain it with a picture{/idea}, in the next verse.
now: You have lived through hard things: a breakup, a layoff, a funeral. You think you know what a terrible day feels like. {trap}This verse says you do not.{/trap} Not to frighten you into despair, but so you prepare properly.
old: I have been through worse days than most people. I can handle anything.
new: No day I have lived compares. I take the warning seriously, and I take hope with it.
try: Ask Allah tonight to make that Day easy for you and the people you love.

title: People scattered like moths, not knowing where to go.
subtitle: The confusion of that Day
then: Ibn Kathir says in their {trap}scattering, dividing, coming and going{/trap}, all bewildered at what is happening, people will be like scattered moths. He compares it to {idea}locusts spread abroad{/idea}.
now: Moths around a porch light at night: frantic, bumping, no direction. That will be people who today walk into meetings with confidence. {idea}The calm you need then is built now{/idea}, in prayers and good deeds.
old: I always know what to do. I am a calm person in a crisis.
new: On that Day everyone is a moth. My steadiness then depends on what I do now.
try: Next time you see moths around a light, recite a short dua for steadiness on the Day.

title: Mountains will float like fluffed wool.
subtitle: The strongest things come apart
then: Ibn Kathir says the mountains will become {trap}like carded wool that has started to wear out and be torn apart{/trap}. Many early scholars said the word means wool. Maududi pairs the two pictures: {idea}people like moths, mountains like wool{/idea}.
now: You lean on things that seem as solid as mountains: a career, a reputation, a country's economy, your own health. On that Day {trap}even mountains drift like fluff{/trap}. What you lean on now should be what lasts.
old: Some things in my life are rock solid.
new: If mountains will drift like wool, only Allah is truly solid to lean on.
try: Name the one thing you lean on most besides Allah. Ask Him to be your first support.

title: Whoever's scale is heavy with good.
subtitle: The balance that decides everything
then: Ibn Kathir says this means {reward}his good deeds are more than his bad deeds{/reward}. After the scenes of confusion, the surah turns to {idea}results: honour or disgrace based on deeds{/idea}.
now: You assume you need a spotless life to be safe, and since you are not spotless, you give up. The verse speaks of {reward}weight, not perfection{/reward}. Every prayer, every kind word, every bit of patience adds to your side.
old: I have done too much wrong for my good to count.
new: It is a scale, not a pass or fail. I can keep adding weight to the good side.
try: Add three things to your good side today, and say astaghfirullah for the other side.

title: A life that pleases the one who lives it.
subtitle: The result of a heavy scale
then: Ibn Kathir says the {reward}pleasant life{/reward} is in Paradise. The word describes a life that is itself pleasing: {idea}a life you would never want to trade{/idea}.
now: You keep thinking you will be happy after the next raise, the next holiday, the next upgrade. Then you want the next one. The verse promises {reward}a life you are fully pleased with{/reward}. That is what the heavy scale buys.
old: Contentment comes when I finally have enough here.
new: Full contentment is waiting for those with a heavy scale. Here I can be patient.
try: Skip one purchase you do not need today and give a little of that money in charity.

title: And whoever's scale is light.
subtitle: The other result
then: Ibn Kathir says this means {trap}his bad deeds are more than his good deeds{/trap}. The surah sets the two outcomes side by side, with nothing in between, so {idea}the listener sees the stakes plainly{/idea}.
now: Think about your last week honestly, like checking a bank statement. More deposits or more withdrawals? {idea}The point is not despair. It is the chance to rebalance while the account is still open.{/idea}
old: I will sort out my balance later in life.
new: My scale is still being filled. Today I can tip it.
try: Think of one wrong you did this week and set it right today, with an apology or a repair.

title: His only home will be the abyss.
subtitle: Why the Fire is called his mother
then: Ibn Jarir said Al-Hawiyah is called {trap}his mother because he will have no other abode{/trap}. Ibn Zayd said it will be his abode, {idea}the place he returns to and settles in{/idea}. Others said it means falling headfirst into it.
now: A mother is where a child runs. The verse uses that word for the opposite: {trap}the only place left to run to{/trap}. It is a hard word, and it is given to you now so you can run to Allah instead, while every door is open.
old: There will always be somewhere to turn.
new: Right now Allah's door is open. I run to Him before there is nowhere else.
try: Make sincere tawbah tonight for one specific thing. Name it to Allah.

title: And what will make you know what it is?
subtitle: The question returns before the answer

row.title: to explain it
sub: the question leads to the meaning

then: The surah opened with a question about the Striker, and now asks the same about the abyss. Ibn Kathir says Allah asks this {idea}in explaining the meaning of Al-Hawiyah{/idea}. The question pauses you {trap}before the last answer{/trap}.
now: You skim warnings: the terms and conditions, the health leaflet, the small print. This verse will not let you skim. {idea}It stops and asks if you really understand.{/idea} The warning is a mercy only if you read it.
old: I get the idea. I do not need the details.
new: Allah pauses me because the warning is meant to change me, not just inform me.
try: Read the whole surah once more today and let it slow you down.

title: A blazing fire. The last word is a warning.
subtitle: Extreme heat, described soberly
then: Ibn Kathir says Hamiyah means {trap}extreme heat with strong flame{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ said the fire people kindle is one part of seventy of it. He also taught that {idea}intense summer heat is a reminder{/idea} from its breath.
now: A heatwave. The car seat burning in July. The oven door opened too fast. Each is a small reminder. Let it turn you, not to fear alone, but to {reward}the One who protects from the Fire{/reward} and to your own deeds.
old: Hot days are just something to complain about.
new: Each hot day can remind me to seek Allah's protection and do good.
try: On the next hot day, say: O Allah, protect me from the Fire.
